construction: Coding clique of size K; q same-index intercluster edges for multiplicity q
decoder: Distinct closed neighborhoods of minimum-degree vertices; cross-cluster edge counts recover multiplicities
proof: For K=p+1, last index has no external neighbors. Minimum degree is K-1. Every vertex of degree K-1 has closed neighborhood equal to its coding clique. Every coding clique supplies such a vertex. Thus decoder recovers all clusters, irrespective of clique number.
conclusion: K>omega is sufficient for coding cliques to be the largest cliques; it is not necessary for lossless decoding. For simple graphs K=2 suffices for this construction regardless of omega.
